title: U.S. House · Illinois's 6th District
area: Western Chicago suburbs in DuPage and Cook counties, including Naperville, Wheaton, Elmhurst, Lombard and Glen Ellyn.

context.text: Incumbent Sean Casten won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary against Joey Ruzevich 75.8%-24.2%. Niki Conforti won the Republican primary against Skylar Duensing 82.2%-17.8%. Heading into 2026, based on the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections, Ballotpedia calculated the district's Cook Partisan Voter Index as D+3.

summary.text: Casten is the Democratic incumbent for Illinois' 6th District, which he has represented since 2019. A scientist and clean-energy executive before entering Congress, he defeated Republican incumbent Peter Roskam in 2018. He sits on the Financial Services Committee and the Joint Economic Committee and won his March 2026 primary with about 76% of the vote.

background.text: Born in Dublin, Ireland, in 1971 to American parents.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Middlebury College (1989). According to his official biography, he holds a Master of Engineering Management and a Master of Science in Biochemical Engineering from Dartmouth College's Thayer School of Engineering (Ballotpedia dates the graduate degree to 1993).
Worked as a scientist at the Tufts School of Medicine and as a clean-energy consultant and manager at Arthur D. Little.

Served as president and CEO of Turbosteam Corporation, which generated heat and power from previously wasted energy, and in 2006 co-founded Recycled Energy Development (Ballotpedia dates the co-founding to 2007).
Was a founding chairman of the Northeast CHP Initiative and chaired the Northeast Combined Heat and Power Association (2005) and the U.S. Combined Heat and Power Association (2007).
Won election to Congress on November 6, 2018, defeating incumbent Republican Peter J. Roskam, and took office in 2019.

Serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the Joint Economic Committee, and as Vice-Chair of the Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition. His official biography says he has held more than 80 town halls.
Won re-election in 2020, 2022 and 2024 and the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary; in 2022 he also defeated then-Rep. Marie Newman in a primary.

priorities.text: Says Congress needs a majority willing to stand up to President Trump on the economy, arguing GDP growth, job creation and falling prices under the Biden administration have slowed or reversed since, largely because of tariffs.
priorities.quote: We know how to fix it; we just need a majority in Congress willing to stand up to the president and for the American people.

priorities.text: Says Congress must assert its oversight powers and reclaim powers taken by the executive branch, including using the power of the purse to withhold funding from agencies that do not comply with ethics rules and the rule of law.
priorities.quote: We must protect our democracy from the harm caused by the Trump administration. Congress needs to not only assert its oversight powers to act as a check but also reclaim powers that were taken by the Executive branch.

priorities.text: Has drafted clean-energy legislation with Rep. Mike Levin (D-CA) that he says would restore incentives previously available under the Inflation Reduction Act and serve as a roadmap for House Democrats' climate and energy policy.
priorities.quote: We must address climate change and remove the barriers to cheap, clean energy deployment. I have drafted legislation to that end with my colleague Mike Levin of California.

positions.summary: Has drafted clean-energy legislation with Rep. Mike Levin that he says would restore Inflation Reduction Act incentives and remove barriers to clean-energy deployment.
positions.quote: We must address climate change and remove the barriers to cheap, clean energy deployment.

positions.summary: Says recent tariffs have contributed to slowing or reversing economic gains, including job creation and falling prices.
positions.quote: All of those trends have slowed or reversed under Donald Trump, largely thanks to unpredictable tariffs and a weakening of the rule of law.

positions.summary: His official issues page says he believes Congress must enshrine the right to an abortion into law.
positions.quote: Rep. Casten believes it is critical that Congress take immediate action to enshrine the right to an abortion into law.

positions.summary: His official issues page says he supports banning semi-automatic weapons with military-style features and strengthening background checks.
positions.quote: Rep. Casten supports banning semi-automatic weapons with military-style features

positions.summary: In a press release he opposed a House Republican bill he said would gut Medicaid and strip coverage from district residents.
positions.quote: The House Republican bill stands to strip over 20,235 people in the 6th Congressional District of their health insurance.

summary.text: Conforti is the Republican nominee for Illinois' 6th District. She describes herself as a businesswoman and energy consultant who previously worked in healthcare administration and owned a staffing business. She ran for this seat in the 2022 primary and the 2024 general election, and won the March 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she is a lifelong resident of the western suburbs of Chicago and a single mother, and comes from a family of military veterans.
Graduated from the University of Chicago School of Economics and earned an M.B.A. in healthcare administration from George Washington University.
According to her campaign website, she grew up in a family-owned business and later owned her own staffing business.
Worked for about 12 years on the administration side of large health systems, including as a director, and says she wrote corporate policy there.
Finished third in the June 2022 Republican primary for this seat with 11.4% of the vote (Keith Pekau won the nomination).
Won the March 2024 Republican primary and lost the November 2024 general election to Sean Casten, 54.2% to 45.8%.
Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 82.2% of the vote over Skylar Duensing.
According to her campaign website, she has been involved in philanthropic efforts through her church and with International Orthodox Christian Charities and Mothers2Mothers.

priorities.text: Says she opposes raising the federal debt ceiling and will push to curb spending, and supports tariffs as a way to bring back manufacturing while pursuing further growth-oriented legislation.
priorities.quote: I am opposed to raising the Debt Ceiling. It will only add to the already enormous burden we are placing on our children and grandchildren.

priorities.text: Says she supports expanding ICE and deporting violent criminals while continuing to support legal immigration.
priorities.quote: I support expanding ICE and deporting violent criminals. Legal immigration is something I fully support.

priorities.text: Describes herself as pro-life with exceptions for rape, incest and the life of the mother, and says she supports the Second Amendment.
priorities.quote: I am proudly Pro-Life with exception (Rape, Incest and the Life of the Mother)... 2nd Amendment I am Pro – 2nd Amendment and believe we must protect our right to bear arms.

positions.summary: Describes herself as pro-life with exceptions for rape, incest and the life of the mother, and criticizes her opponent's support for abortion access.
positions.quote: I am proudly Pro-Life with exception (Rape, Incest and the Life of the Mother), and I oppose the Democrats' radical abortion agenda.

positions.summary: Supports expanding ICE and deporting violent criminals, while saying she supports legal immigration.
positions.quote: I support expanding ICE and deporting violent criminals.

positions.summary: Says tariffs will help bring back manufacturing and add jobs, though more is needed to stimulate economic growth.
positions.quote: Tariffs will help bring back manufacturing and add jobs, but more needs to be done.
